Police and prosecutors had asked for help in finding Ballout, but warned the public to avoid “direct contact” with him, saying he may be armed and dangerous. 

Police searched an apartment in the Schöneberg district of Berlin near the scene of the attack in the early hours of Sunday, but said they had found no one there.

Describing Ballout as “generous, emotional, loving”, he said his son had lived with his mother, from whom Tawfik is divorced, and two of his three sisters. Ballout attended school until 10th grade, then bounced from job to job, in security or as a driver.

Tawfik described the family as Shia but “not extremely religious” and said it “does not support Islamic State”, an extremist Sunni group.

Police said the vehicle had struck multiple ⁠people after being driven into the Tiergarten. Shortly before 10pm the driver of the white minivan swerved into the park, close to where the route of the Pride march had been earlier in the day, hitting people on a path and crashing into a tree.

Bild cited a witness as saying that a man had emerged from the vehicle and fled on foot. A hunt involving helicopters and officers from several German states was under way across the capital on Sunday.

Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered in Berlin in warm summer sunshine to celebrate the Pride parade. It is known in Germany as Christopher Street Day (CSD), named after the site of the Stonewall Inn in New York City where riots against police raids touched off the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement. CSD was first held in West Berlin in 1979.

Berlin’s mayor, Kai Wegner, called the deadly assault “an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society”.

The parade on Saturday ran under the motto “taking a stand is hot”, which organisers said was “in response to increasing hostility” to LGBTQ+ people in Germany.

More than 80 floats and 50 groups on foot joined the procession through the city centre past Potsdamer Platz and the Victory Column monument in the Tiergarten, culminating in a rally at the Brandenburg Gate.

Before last year’s parade, Berlin LGBTQ+ organisations sounded the alarm that attacks had become more frequent while hard-won rights were under threat. Campaigners said a rise in hostility had accompanied the surge in support for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), now the most popular party in national opinion polls, as well as an increase in Islamist-inspired attacks.

Far-right leaders were also quick to comment on the attacks. The co-leader of the AfD Tino Chrupalla wrote on X: “We declare the war against Islamists. We will not allow religious extremists to divide our country with violence and intolerance!”

The president of the French far-right National Rally, Jordan Bardella, wrote: “The Islamist threat remains a major issue in Europe and continues to target what they hate most about our civilisation – and what we cherish so much – freedom.”

🎙 Up to 6 million Iranian pilgrims expected to attend Arbaeen march: Official

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The head of the representative office of Iran’s Hajj and Pilgrimage Organization in Iraq has forecast that between five and six million Iranian pilgrims will take part in this year’s Arbaeen march.

Speaking to the Iraqi official news agency (INA), Mohsen Esmail Sagharchi said on Monday night that the brotherly relations and solidarity between the Iraqi and Iranian peoples would contribute to the expected turnout.
​
He added that during Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi’s recent visit to Iraq, coordination was carried out with Iraqi officials and relevant authorities over logistical support and necessary measures inside the country.
​
The Iranian official said the Islamic Republic will participate in the Arbaeen pilgrimage by operating around 3,000 service stations – known as mokeb – at Iraq’s holy sites.
​
He added that the governors of Najaf and Karbala had pledged to provide fuel quotas for those service stations, well as other necessary logistical support to help serve Iranian pilgrims.
​
Arbaeen marks the 40th day after Ashura, which commemorates the martyrdom of Imam Hussein (PBUH), the third Shia Imam.
​
Every year, millions of pilgrims from Iran and other Muslim countries travel to Iraq to take part in the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, many of them making the journey on foot to the holy city of Karbala, home to the shrine of Imam Hussein (PBUH). This year, Arbaeen falls on August 4.
